free_tier.stated: NO TOTAL QUOTA — read verbatim from Commons:Maximum_file_size: 'there is no limit to the *total* size of uploads by an individual account.' Per-file cap is 5 GiB (5,368,709,120 bytes) via chunked upload, 100 MiB otherwise. Live API confirms: `maxuploadsize: 5368709120`.

egress.terms: free, unmetered, CDN (upload.wikimedia.org), no auth, Range supported. Wikimedia runs its own edge cache in front of Swift.

interface_detail: MediaWiki Action API + REST; `action=upload` with `stash`/`filekey` for chunked; `upload_by_url` right for server-side upload
tooling: mwclient / pywikibot / commons-cli; `upload` and `upload_by_url` are granted to the plain `user` group (verified in siteinfo usergroups), so a brand-new account can already do server-side upload without waiting
chaining: `upload_by_url` means Commons fetches the file from YOUR url — no local bandwidth at all. Files land at upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/<x>/<xy>/<name>, hash-addressed and immutably versioned.
limits_note: 5 GiB/file, 100 MiB without chunking; per-licence/scope review at the community level; thumbnailing capped at a 59 s timeout, 100 MP for GIFs

identity_cost.detail: email — account is username+password+email, no affiliation. Note the nuance: upload itself is in the base `user` group, but `reupload` (overwrite) needs autoconfirmed. So first uploads are open; overwriting an existing file needs account age.

reliability_note: The one platform here where a multi-TB batch is explicitly contemplated — Commons asks you to warn sysadmins before 'batch uploads amounting to several TB', which is an acknowledgement that people do it.
confidence_note: One page read moves it to documented.

evidence.proved: same API with siprop=usergroups — `user` group holds ['upload','upload_by_url','reupload-own','move-categorypages']
